newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling strengthens marginally vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling strengthens marginally vs dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling gained marginally against the dollar on Tuesday, boosted by moderate exporter sales amid poor demand, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean commercial rate of 59.01 against the dollar compared to 59.21 on Monday. Against the pound, the shilling was posted at a mean rate of 99.04 from 99.33.
"We've seen the shilling post some gains this morning. There was an inflow of dollars from local exporters," a dealer said.
Another dealer said sentiment appeared to have changed in favour of a stronger shilling. "We've got good orders for dollars but nobody wants to buy above the 59 level," he said.
At midday brokers said they were selling dollars at 59.10-58.99 from opening rates of 59.25-59.40. But the dealers said at 59 the shilling was bound to experience some resistance.
"Every time it touches 59 a lot of the big buyers come in and drive rates up again," one dealer said.
The money market remained liquid with overnight rates quoted at 5-8 percent unchanged.
